Bank holiday today: Are banks open or closed in your state today on November 11, 2026?
 By Sneha Kulkarni , ET Online Last Updated: Nov 11, 2026, 07:00:00 AM IST Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis
 On November 11, 2026, banks will observe holidays in specific states for various regional festivals. These festivals include Laxmi Puja, Ningol Chakkouba, and Bhai Dooj. Some states will continue to operate normally despite these closures. Bank customers should confirm the holiday schedule before visiting their local branches. Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen ET Online ​Are banks open or closed in your state today?​ If you are planning a bank visit today (Wednesday, November 11, 2026), check the state-wise bank holiday list before stepping out. Banks will remain closed in select states on Wednesday to mark different regional festivals, including Laxmi Puja (Deepawali), Ningol Chakkouba, Bhai Dooj and Chitragupt Jayanti.
However, the holiday will not apply uniformly across the country, and bank branches in other states will stay open. Here is a look at the places where banks will remain closed on November 11. Also find out the bank holiday calendar for this month (November 2026).
 Bank holiday on November 11, 2026
Banks will be closed on November 11, 2026, to celebrate Laxmi Puja (Deepawali)/Ningol Chakkouba/Bhratridwitiya/Bhaidooj/Chitragupt Jayanti in Sikkim, Manipur, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Himachal Pradesh. 
 November 2026 bank holiday occasions
Diwali/Laxmi Puj/Govardhan Pooja/Vishwakarma Day, Diwali (Bali Pratipada)/Deepawali (Govardhan Puja)/Laxmi Puja/Vikram Samvant New Year Day, Laxmi Puja (Deepawali)/Ningol Chakkouba/Bhratridwitiya/Bhaidooj/Chitragupt Jayanti, Wangala Festival, Chhath Puja/Surya Shashti Dala Chhath (Prath Arghya), Igas-Bagwal, Seng Kut Snem, Guru Nanak Jayanti/Karthika Purnima/ Rahas Purnima and Kanakadasa Jayanthi.
In India, all scheduled and non-scheduled banks observe public holidays on the second and fourth Saturdays. The first, third and fifth (in some cases) remain a working Saturday for banks unless specified in the RBI holiday calendar.
